message.content:
The quadratic equation is  

\[
x^2 + 2x + 3 = 0 .
\]

Using the quadratic formula  

\[
x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{\,b^{2}-4ac\,}}{2a},
\]

with \(a=1,\; b=2,\; c=3\):

1. Compute the discriminant  
   \[
   \Delta = b^{2}-4ac = 2^{2}-4(1)(3)=4-12=-8 .
   \]

2. Take the square root of the discriminant  
   \[
   \sqrt{\Delta} = \sqrt{-8}= \sqrt{8}\,i = 2\sqrt{2}\,i .
   \]

3. Plug into the formula  
   \[
   x = \frac{-2 \pm 2\sqrt{2}\,i}{2}
     = -1 \pm \sqrt{2}\,i .
   \]

So the two (complex) solutions are  

\[
\boxed{x = -1 + i\sqrt{2}\quad\text{and}\quad x = -1 - i\sqrt{2}} .
\]

There are no real roots because the discriminant is negative.
